name: What should be included in a gut renovation estimate?

mainEntity.name: What line items should a detailed gut-renovation quote in Los Angeles include?
mainEntity.text: What line items should a detailed gut-renovation quote in Los Angeles include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful gut-renovation estimate should break out the full scope so the homeowner can compare bids fairly. At minimum, it should include demolition and debris hauling, permit and inspection costs, design and engineering coordination, structural framing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, insulation, drywall, flooring, tile, cabinetry, countertops, paint, fixtures, and final cleanup. It should also identify exclusions such as appliances, landscaping, utility upgrades, or temporary housing. In Los Angeles, the best estimates often note assumptions about existing conditions, material allowances, and allowance values for finishes. If a quote is too vague, it becomes hard to tell whether one contractor is truly cheaper or simply leaving out expensive parts of the job. A strong estimate also states how change orders are priced, because this is where many budgets drift upward. Ask for a scope sheet and an allowance schedule before signing.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detailed gut-renovation estimate should include demolition, hauling, permits, architectural and engineering work, structural framing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, insulation, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, finishes, inspections, and contingency assumptions. Vague lump-sum quotes can hide exclusions and make it hard to compare bids accurately.
